name: Stability AI
description: Read-only Stability AI account surface: account identity and organisation memberships, the API key's credit balance, and the engines the key is allowed to use. NO GENERATION TOOL IS EXPOSED, deliberately: every Stability image, video and upscale endpoint is a POST that spends credits, so this connector carries no generation call at all and cannot spend money.

tools.name: account
tools.description: Get the Stability AI account the API key belongs to: user id, email and every organisation the user is a member of

tools.name: balance
tools.description: Get the credit balance of the Stability AI account or organisation the API key is scoped to

organization_id.description: Optional Stability organisation ID to read the balance of (e.g. org-123456). Defaults to the user's default organisation.

tools.name: list_engines
tools.description: List the Stability AI engines (models) available to the account, with the content type each one produces

organization_id.description: Optional Stability organisation ID to list engines for (e.g. org-123456). Defaults to the user's default organisation.

needs_review: READ-ONLY BY DESIGN, AND FOR COST REASONS: no tool is marked write:true and no generation endpoint is present. Stability's text-to-image, image-to-image, upscale, video and 3D endpoints are all POSTs that consume credits from the same key, so exposing one would let an agent spend the customer's money. Only the three metered-at-zero read endpoints are wired: /v1/user/account, /v1/user/balance and /v1/engines/list.

list_engines uses a ROOT-ARRAY pick ('[]'). Documented shape: ListEnginesResponseBody is declared type 'array' of Engine {id, name, description, type} in the OpenAPI document embedded in https://platform.stability.ai/docs/api-reference, NOT an object with an 'engines' key.

The optional 'Organization' request header on balance and list_engines is documented (components.parameters.organization, in: header, name: Organization) and is dropped by the declarative runtime when the caller omits organization_id. The shape-proof harness does not send per-tool request headers, so the header path itself is NOT covered by the proof run; the default no-header path is.

auth kept as scaffolded (bearer api_key) and confirmed against the live host: /v1/user/account, /v1/user/balance and /v1/engines/list each answer a dummy bearer with a structured JSON 401 {id, name, message}, while a bogus path on the same host answers 404 with an empty body.
